module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 180

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/180)
- [ErSi82] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*.
  Combinatorica (1982), 275-288.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos180

/-- A finite graph, bundled with its vertex count, so that a family may mix orders. -/
structure FiniteGraph where
  order : ℕ
  graph : SimpleGraph (Fin order)

/-- A host graph is `family`-free when it contains no member of `family` as a subgraph. -/
def FamilyFree (family : Finset FiniteGraph) {n : ℕ} (host : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ forbidden ∈ family, forbidden.graph.Free host

open scoped Classical in
/-- $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$, the greatest number of edges of a graph on `n` vertices
containing no member of `family`. -/
noncomputable def familyExtremal (family : Finset FiniteGraph) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (FamilyFree family)).sup
    fun host : SimpleGraph (Fin n) => host.edgeFinset.card

/-- No member of the family is acyclic. -/
def IsCyclicFamily (family : Finset FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ forbidden ∈ family, ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic

/-- The family is *compact*: some single member already controls the family extremal number. -/
def IsCompactFamily (family : Finset FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ forbidden ∈ family, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (extremalNumber n forbidden.graph : ℝ) ≤ C * (familyExtremal family n : ℝ)

/--
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set of finite graphs then $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum
number of edges a graph on $n$ vertices can have without containing any subgraphs from
$\mathcal{F}$. Note that it is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})\leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for
every $G\in\mathcal{F}$. Is it true that, for every $\mathcal{F}$, there exists $G\in\mathcal{F}$
such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll_{\mathcal{F}}\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})?$$

This is the Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture. The answer is no: OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a
family of connected bipartite graphs, none of them acyclic, for which no single member controls
the family extremal number. See `erdos_180.variants.counterexample`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_180 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family → IsCompactFamily family := by
  sorry

/--
The counterexample: a nonempty family of connected bipartite graphs, none acyclic, that is not
compact.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs/blob/94bc0feb6a9ff12c7d31d6de640a725c9d43d2b6/CompactnessAndDegeneracy.lean"]
theorem erdos_180.variants.counterexample :
    ∃ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty ∧
      (∀ forbidden ∈ family,
        forbidden.graph.Connected ∧ forbidden.graph.IsBipartite ∧
          ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic) ∧
      ¬ IsCompactFamily family := by
  sorry

end Erdos180

findings.description: The theorem docstring quotes the literal erdosproblems question, "Is it true that, for every F, there exists G∈F such that ex(n;G) ≪_F ex(n;F)?". The Lean statement quantifies only over families with `family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family →`, i.e. nonempty families in which no member is a forest. The docstring never mentions or explains this restriction. It also leaves out the folklore counterexample that forces it: as literally stated, the question fails trivially for {K_{1,2}, 2K_2}. The mathematics is fine; the restricted form is the intended corrected conjecture (see reformulations). But the docstring states a different, broader question than the Lean. AGENTS.md asks that a non-obvious domain restriction be explained.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/180 (LaTeX source at /latex/180): "Hunter has provided the following 'folklore counterexample': if F={H_1,H_2} where H_1 is a star and H_2 is a matching, both with at least two edges, then ex(n;F)≪1, but ex(n;H_i)≍n ... This conjecture may still hold for all other F." Wigderson's note "The Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture needs more assumptions" (https://ywigderson.math.ethz.ch/math/static/Compactness.pdf) gives Simonovits' modified form: "For every finite collection F of graphs which contains no forest ...". OpenAI, Ten Advances, Ch. 10 §1.1: "The corrected form of the conjecture (see [Wig]) asks: for every finite nonempty family of graphs F, all of whose members contain cycles, ...".
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the docstring of `erdos_180`: "As literally stated the question fails for the folklore family {K_{1,2}, 2K_2} (a star and a matching). Following Simonovits' corrected form (see Wigderson's note and [OpenAI26, (1)]), we formalise it for nonempty families none of whose members is a forest (`IsCyclicFamily`)." Optionally cite Wigderson's note in the module references.

reformulations.difference: The source literally asks, for every finite family F, whether some G∈F has ex(n;G) ≪_F ex(n;F). The Lean has three differences. (a) It quantifies only over nonempty families none of whose members is acyclic (`IsCyclicFamily`, i.e. no member is a forest). (b) It writes ≪_F as ∃ C>0 with ex(n;G) ≤ C·ex(n;F) for all sufficiently large n (`∀ᶠ n in atTop`). (c) It fixes the answer as `answer(False)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
The Lean universal is not equivalent to the literal 'for every F' universal: that one is refuted outright by {K_{1,2}, 2K_2}, which the source itself records. It is equivalent to the version the source leaves open ('this conjecture may still hold for all other F'), i.e. over families not of star-plus-matching type.

Suppose F contains a forest T. Then one of three things holds.
(i) Some member G0 has at most one edge. Then ex(n;G0)=0 for large n, so F is compact via G0.
(ii) F has no member all of whose edges share a vertex, so the star K_{1,n-1} is F-free. Or F has no member of maximum degree ≤1, so a maximum matching is F-free. Either way ex(n;F)=Ω(n) ≥ ex(n;T)/C, because forests have ex=O(n), so F is compact via T.
(iii) F contains both a star-like and a matching-like member with ≥2 edges. This is exactly the folklore type the source excludes.
So 'every non-folklore F is compact' ⟺ 'every nonempty cyclic F is compact'. This matches Simonovits' corrected conjecture ('F contains no forest', per Wigderson) and OpenAI's (1).

Nonemptiness is implicit: '∃ G∈F' fails for F=∅. 'Eventually' is equivalent to 'for all n': when every member contains a cycle, ex(n;F) ≥ n−1 ≥ 1 for n≥2, since a star is F-free; and ex(n;·)=0 for n≤1. So finitely many n can be absorbed into C.

The erdosproblems DB counts OpenAI's `not_erdos_180 : ¬CompactnessConjectureStatement` as the Lean disproof of #180. That is literally this statement, with identical definitions. The fixed answer(False) is correct under either reading.

review.notes:
Both declarations say what the sources say.

- **Main theorem.** `erdos_180` is `False ↔ ∀ family, family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family → IsCompactFamily family`. This is exactly the negation of OpenAI's `CompactnessConjectureStatement`, and all five helper definitions are verbatim copies of OpenAI's. OpenAI's statement is the corrected Erdős–Simonovits conjecture ("no forest in F", Simonovits via Wigderson). The erdosproblems DB accepts `not_erdos_180` as the Lean disproof of #180.
- **Variant.** `erdos_180.variants.counterexample` matches OpenAI's Theorem 1.1 and the #575 remark (connected bipartite members, each containing a cycle, not compact), without the quantitative exponents.
- **Definitions.** I checked the Mathlib ones used: `Free` (no non-induced copy), `extremalNumber` (sup of edge counts, 0 on the empty set), `IsAcyclic`, `IsBipartite` (`Colorable 2`) and `Connected`. `answer(False)` elaborates to `False`.
- **Scratch proofs.** These compiled: the variant implies the negative answer to the main question; singleton families have `familyExtremal = extremalNumber` and are compact, so `IsCompactFamily` is not vacuous; the empty family is never compact.
- **Status.** `research solved` with `answer(False)` matches erdosproblems' "DISPROVED (LEAN)", so there is nothing to report.
- **`formal_proof` link.** I did not rebuild it: ten-proofs pins Lean v4.32.0 and its own Mathlib, while the sandbox is on v4.33.1. The linked file has no `sorry`, `axiom`, `admit` or `native_decide`. Its `formalization.yaml` reports 0 sorries and only standard axioms for `CompactnessConjecture.quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample`, which implies both FC declarations.
- **Optional metadata.** `erdos_180` itself carries no `formal_proof` attribute, although `CompactnessConjecture.not_erdos_180` proves exactly it.
- **Sources I could not use directly.** The UCSD graph-problems page (#47) writes the inequality the trivial way round (t(n,F)=O(t(n,G))); the FC file correctly follows erdosproblems' nontrivial direction. The original ES82 paper at renyi.hu is a scan with no text layer, so I could not read it; Wigderson's note quotes its Conjecture 1 ("for every finite collection F ... ex(n,F) ≥ c·ex(n,H) for all n").
